system.name: Claims Copilot
system.purpose: Summarize claim files and draft adjuster recommendations; humans approve all claim decisions.
system.data: Claim notes, policy text, customer PII, medical and payment information

genai_tests.observation: Indirect instructions in retrieved claim notes overrode task constraints.
Cross-claim identifiers appeared in two adversarial retrieval tests.
Unsupported policy-limit statements were produced without citations.
No material system instruction disclosure observed.
The assistant cannot approve or pay claims and requires adjuster confirmation.

evidence.title: Architecture and data-flow diagram
evidence.description: Approved diagram showing retrieval boundary, identity controls, logging, and provider connection.

evidence.title: Red-team test results
evidence.description: Dated test workbook with prompts, expected behavior, actual output, and reviewer disposition for 110 cases.

evidence.title: Human oversight procedure
evidence.description: Procedure requiring adjusters to verify citations and approve every recommendation.

sample_conclusion: Claims Copilot is fully compliant with NIST AI RMF and ISO/IEC 42001. The control environment is effective and ineffective. Prompt injection presents a Critical risk. Testing proves that customer data will never be disclosed. EV-001 supports this conclusion.
